_why: ADR 0141's TYPESCRIPT half, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
Two defects, one cause: `report` read quantities with `Number()` instead
of the parser every other command uses. `Number('10mM')` is NaN, and a
bare `--vmax 0.25` was used as mM/s while parseQuantity assumes uM/min --
the same three characters, 60,000x apart, decided by which command read
them. A wrong Vmax does not fail; it produces a plausible trajectory in
a document meant for a teacher.
Split from the Python half (adr-0141-payload-guard.json): a set has one
test command, and this ADR's evidence spans jest and pytest.

mutations.description: s0 is read with Number() again
mutations._note: The original defect. `Number('10mM')` is NaN, JSON.stringify writes null, and the value disappears before anything can complain.
mutations.replace: const parsed = { value: Number(s0Raw), unit: 'mM', unitDeclared: true };

mutations.description: a bare vmax is used as mM/s instead of converted from uM/min
mutations._note: The 60,000x error. The test pins it as a number rather than as a policy, because a policy assertion would pass on any conversion.

mutations.description: an assumed unit is no longer recorded as assumed
mutations._note: parseQuantity already separates a unit the user declared from one it chose. That is the provenance argument applied to units, and flattening it at the CLI boundary loses it for the document.
mutations.find:
basis: raw['s0-basis'],
        assumedUnit: parsed.unitDeclared ? undefined : parsed.unit,
